1. TASK_QUEUE.md reads as one document, not a patch. The new status:"blocked" block (lines 422-465) sits immediately after the existing status:"done" paragraph and before the two pre-existing bash examples, at the same heading depth (bold-lead-sentence-then-prose, same voice as the done paragraph immediately above it, same citation style '(see X, above)' / '(see Y below)' used throughout the rest of the file). It reuses the file's established rhetorical device of naming a real incident as evidence (task 458/ISS-0458), matching how the done-paragraph above it cites #360/#366/#367/ISS-0277. The new 'What status:"blocked" does NOT assert' paragraph explicitly reconciles with the document's own earlier use of the word 'blocked' ('report blocked, do not select') rather than silently introducing a second, colliding sense of the same word -- this is exactly the kind of internal-consistency care a bolted-on patch would skip. Verdict: PASS, reads as one document.

2. Cross-reference correctness and no drift between TASK_QUEUE.md and ISSUE_QUEUE.md. TASK_QUEUE.md's new block cites ISSUE_QUEUE.md's 'Issue status vocabulary' by name and correctly attributes instrumented/no_defect's defining properties (instrumented: verified work shipped, root cause open, required superseded_by:; no_defect: investigated/measured, no root cause) -- checked against ISSUE_QUEUE.md's actual bullets (lines ~190-238) and these match verbatim in substance. ISSUE_QUEUE.md's two new sentences (end of instrumented bullet, end of no_defect bullet's evidence-bar paragraph) both say 'release_lock(status: "blocked")... see TASK_QUEUE.md's release_lock section for why' -- consistent word-for-word between the two insertion points, and consistent with what TASK_QUEUE.md's block actually says (excludes from get_next_task claims, does not close the GitHub issue). The `resolved` bullet is correctly left untouched, matching the design's explicit instruction not to touch it. No drift found in either direction. Verdict: PASS.

3. WF-03_issue_resolving.md Step 5 mirrors the existing GitHub-close-comment branch correctly. Read lines 154-228 in full. Step 5 section 2 (lines 179-194) branches the GitHub close --comment text three ways (resolved/instrumented/no_defect) with an indented arrow-style block. The rewritten ORCH release_lock instruction (lines 206-226) uses the identical structural device -- a two-line indented arrow block ('resolved -> release_lock(status: "done")' / 'instrumented / no_defect -> release_lock(status: "blocked")') immediately after stating the branch is keyed off 'THE SAME local docs/issues/ISS-NNNN.yaml status this step's §1 just wrote,' explicitly tying it back to §1's status line rather than re-deriving it. Read as a whole step (not just the inserted clause): the paragraph flows grammatically from 'call release_lock against that task id' through the branch table through the reasoning paragraph through the unchanged unreachable-queue fallback sentence -- no dangling referent, no leftover singular-status assumption elsewhere in the step. The old unconditional 'call release_lock with status:"done"' sentence is fully replaced, not left as a stray duplicate. Verdict: PASS.

Its Decision/Consequences sections name exactly which TASK_QUEUE.md sections it will rewrite: Hard Rule, set_lock, 'A human names a specific issue,' reachability-checks, and the 'four functions' heading/framing -- confirmed by re-reading those live sections (lines 1-125, 380-420) that none of them have been touched by this commit and none of 0017's own rewrite has landed yet either (both are still pending, independently). No conflict with 0017 found in the implemented text. Verdict: PASS, independently re-derived, not copied from step-02's design claim.

Queue task 458 was NOT re-released in this step, correctly deferred to ORCH per the handoff's own point 5 and the design's AC3 recommendation. Verdict: PASS.

Residual 'exactly four operations' framing: FOUND, two instances, both pre-existing (not introduced or touched by this commit) and both in TASK_QUEUE.md, the file this run does own: line 118 ('the service is deliberately four operations... exactly four endpoints, on purpose' -- inside the reconciliation-fallback bash comment) and line 386 ('the service is deliberately four operations, per its own README's "Design" section' -- inside the 'A human names a specific issue' section, one of the exact sections 0017's own Consequences list names for rewrite).
